subject: Possible to implement Gibbs Sampler with Metropolis Step in STAN?

messages.author: f1f93de00b458a56
messages.subject: Possible to implement Gibbs Sampler with Metropolis Step in STAN?
parts:
Hi,

I'm working on a causal inference problem that is similar to the problem solved in Hirano, Imbens, Rubin and Zhou (2000) "Estimating the Effect of Flu Shots in a Random Encouragement Design" (which is also discussed in Chapter 25 of the Imbens and Rubin "Causal Inference" book). Basically, the problem is to get a posterior for the complier average causal effect (CACE) using data from a randomized experiment with two way non-compliance. 

This would be very easy to implement in STAN if I could observe the complete data likelihood, where I know the compliance status of the experimental units (whether they always take treatment regardless of assignment, never take treatment regardless of assignment, or whether they take the treatment to which they were randomly assigned). 

The usual way to do this would be to set up a gibbs sampler where I draw the latent variables of interest conditional on some covariates and my parameter vector, then draw the missing potential outcomes conditional on some covariates, the latent variable and my parameter vector, and then update my parameter vector with an annoying metropolis step. 

I would prefer not to write customized MCMC code for this, mostly to avoid the pain of exploring tuning parameters for the metropolis step.

Is there a way to leverage STAN for these types of problems? Basically, using it for the metropolis step somehow? Or can I scrap the gibbs sampler approach and deal with latent variables in some other fashion in STAN?

Any help would be greatly appreciated. 

Thanks!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Possible to implement Gibbs Sampler with Metropolis Step in STAN?
parts:
If the latent parameters are continuous, this is straightforward
in Stan (not "STAN" --- it's not an acronym). See the missing data
chapter of the manual.

If they are binary or small categorical, they can be marginalized out,
which is more work. See the latent discrete parameter chapter of the manual.

If they're counts, it's pretty much impossible to do in Stan without
approximating the model somehow.

- Bob
